body_text:
An infinite series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n$ converges to sum
$S \in \mathbb{R}$ if the sequence of partial sums
$s_N = \sum_{n=1}^N a_n$ converges to $S$ as $N \to \infty$.

An infinite sum is thus fundamentally defined as the limit of
finite algebraic sums. A necessary condition for convergence is
that the terms vanish: $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = 0$. However,
this condition is famously insufficient: the Harmonic Series
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n}$ diverges to infinity despite
its terms tending to zero.
